meta.purpose: Breaks the consumer PWA (Docs/22 W- screens, WP19 'Consumer PWA') into stages that can each run in a fresh context. Each stage reports back into this file, so the next context knows what is done, what changed, and what to watch out for.
how_to_use: Start a new context with: 'Run stage <id> of pwa/dev_plan.json' (ids are P1..P13; backend stages are always written 'backend S<n>' to avoid confusion).

Read this file first: global_decisions, conventions, doc_issues, backend_readiness, the reports of all completed stages, handoff_notes and open_questions. Then read only the doc sections listed in the stage's context_to_read.

Check backend readiness before a stage that depends on it: read backend/dev_plan.json meta.progress, or run `pnpm contract:coverage` in backend/. If a needed backend stage is not done, build the screens against the contract, show the 'not available yet' state for 501 responses (GD-13), and list the gap in the stage report.

Before starting, set the stage status to 'in_progress' and fill report.started_at. Update each task's status as you go (not_started | in_progress | done | deferred | blocked), so a context that runs out mid-stage can be resumed.

When finishing, fill the stage report (summary, screens_done, deviations, notes_for_next, tests_after_stage), set status to 'done' (or 'partial' with reasons), append to handoff_notes and deviations_log, update meta.progress and screen_coverage, and set meta.last_updated.
Never delete earlier reports. Correct them by appending a note that says what changed.
If a stage changes a global decision, add an amendment to that decision with the stage id and a reason. Do not edit the decision in place without a trace.

If a stage must change backend code (e.g. DI-08 storage CORS), keep the change minimal, add tests in backend/, run the backend checks, and record it in both this file (deviations_log) and backend/dev_plan.json (handoff_notes).

global_decisions.decision: One Next.js app (App Router, React Server Components, TypeScript strict, ESM) in pwa/, managed by pnpm with its own lockfile (no root workspace, so backend/ stays untouched). Styling with Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first config). Exact versions are the current stable releases at P1 install time and are recorded in the P1 report.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/02 §2 names React + Next.js + Tailwind for the consumer PWA (SSR for public SEO pages). A standalone package mirrors backend/ and avoids reworking the backend's install.

global_decisions.decision: Node: the PWA runs on the project-local Node 24 that backend/ already installed. pwa/tools/use-local-node.sh and use-local-node.ps1 put backend/.tools/node first on PATH (and run backend's setup script if it is missing). pwa/.node-version = 24.21.0.
global_decisions.reason: System Node must stay 20.10 (backend environment note). One local Node for both packages avoids a second download.

global_decisions.decision: The consumer BFF (Docs/41 D4/G2, Docs/40 SEC-WEB) is built inside the PWA as server-only code (pwa/src/server/bff/) mounted by Next.js route handlers: /api/v1/[...path] (1:1 forwarder), /bff/login, /bff/oauth/callback, /bff/logout, /bff/session, /bff/csrf. The BFF code is written over standard Request/Response with no Next.js imports, so it can later move to backend/api-gateway/ unchanged.
global_decisions.reason: SEC-WEB-1/2 require a same-origin BFF that holds the tokens; backend/dev_plan.json defers BFFs to backend/api-gateway 'later' and none of backend S7-S9 builds them. Building it with the PWA is the only way to make the PWA work, and keeping it framework-free keeps the Docs/41 placement possible.

global_decisions.decision: Contract types are generated, never hand-written. pwa/tools/contract/generate.ts reads backend/libs/contract/generated/{operations.json,schemas.json,operation-schemas.json,enums.ts,errors.ts} and writes shared/api-contracts/generated/ (operation map: opId → method, path template, path params, query, input/response TypeScript types, sec tags such as IDEM/ETAG/AAL2/FLAG; enums; error codes). `pnpm contract:generate` regenerates; `pnpm contract:check` fails when stale. The PWA imports it through a linked package (@carpal/api-contracts, 'link:../shared/api-contracts').
global_decisions.reason: Docs/02 §6.1 'strict API contracts: TypeScript clients generated into shared/api-contracts; a breaking API change fails the PWA build'. The backend's OpenAPI file is a backend S9 item, but its generated registry already exists and is checked against Docs/40.

amendments.change: shared/api-contracts/openapi.yaml now exists (backend S9c, GD-37; written and checked only by backend `pnpm openapi:check`). The server-defined Json<…> shapes (MatchReasonValues, FeedCard, TemplateParams, InsightPayload, SuggestionPayload, WebAuthn option/credential JSON …; backend DI-50) are taken from the OpenAPI components, so the generator reads openapi.yaml for those types only. amendments.reason: BA-24; avoids two writers of shared/api-contracts and closes the x-server-schema gap.

global_decisions.decision: Hosted sign-in UI (Docs/40 §6.2 'hosted sign-in UI on id.carpal.app', screens of W-AUTH-01 / S-AUTH-02,03,07,08,09) is built in the PWA codebase as its own route group (/id/signin/...). Dev topology: the PWA proxies /id/oauth/*, /id/v1/auth/* and /id/.well-known/* to the auth host (127.0.0.1:8082), so the hosted UI and the auth endpoints share one origin and the interaction cookie is first-party. Backend env for dev: CARPAL_SIGNIN_URL=http://localhost:3000/id/signin and CARPAL_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URIS={"cp-web-consumer":["http://localhost:3000/bff/oauth/callback"]}. The BFF exchanges codes and refresh tokens server-to-server directly with :8082.
global_decisions.reason: The interaction cookie is set by the auth host, so the sign-in page must be on the same origin as /v1/auth/*. No sign-in UI exists in backend/. Production placement (id.carpal.app served from the PWA build, or a separate small app) is OQ-03.

amendments.change: Dev backend env (backend/.env, loaded by `pnpm dev`) also needs CARPAL_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=localhost and CARPAL_WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS=["http://localhost:3000"] (defaults are carpal.app and https origins; passkeys are now implemented, BA-09). Completion of the hosted UI re-requests the same /oauth/authorize URL (cookie-bound interaction); an unknown or expired interaction answers 410 LINK_EXPIRED, which the hosted UI turns into 'This sign-in page expired' plus a restart of /bff/login with the same return URL (BA-12). /oauth/token errors are RFC 6749 JSON (ProtocolError), not problem+json; the BFF maps both. DPoP proofs sent to /oauth/token must use htu = <issuer>/oauth/token (issuer from the discovery document), even though the BFF connects to 127.0.0.1:8082 (DI-17, GD-07 amendment).
amendments.reason: BA-09, BA-12; verified in backend/libs/config/config.ts and modules/identity/application/auth-server.ts on 2026-10-25.

amendments.change: Dev values as built: redirect URI https://localhost:3000/bff/oauth/callback (Url is https-only, DI-24), CARPAL_SIGNIN_URL=https://localhost:3000/id/signin (optional: the proxy rewrites issuer redirects to <origin>/id), CARPAL_WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS=["https://localhost:3000"]. CARPAL_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URIS replaces the whole map, so it lists the other clients' defaults too (pwa/README.md, backend/.env.example comment). The /id proxy exposes auth.authorize, auth.pow_challenge, discovery, JWKS and every /v1/auth/* operation, never /oauth/token or /oauth/revoke; it passes only the __Host-cp_ia cookie in both directions.
amendments.reason: DI-24; keeps the BFF the only token client.

global_decisions.decision: 'Intent survives sign-in' (Docs/22 principle 2) is done with a context modal plus a redirect, not a credentials modal: a gated action opens a small modal ('Sign in to follow Reza Auto Suspension') with Log in / Sign up; the action (type, target, return URL, form draft) is stored server-side in the BFF pre-session (TTL 30 min, size-capped), the browser goes through the hosted sign-in, and on return the page replays the action once and shows its toast.
global_decisions.reason: Credentials must be entered on the hosted sign-in origin (GD-05; frame-ancestors 'none' forbids an iframe). Logged as DI-01.

global_decisions.decision: Tokens per audience: (a) signed-in browser sessions use the user's cp-web-consumer tokens (refresh rotated in the BFF; a refresh-reuse error ends the session); (b) guests get an anonymous cp-web-consumer token (scope 'public.read search', 15 min, no refresh) created lazily per pre-session (SEC-AU-14); (c) server rendering of public pages uses a cached cp-ssr client-credentials token (public.read). Every BFF call sends CarPal-Client 'cp-web-consumer/<version> (web 1.0)' (or cp-ssr), Accept-Language from the URL locale, and CarPal-Timezone from the browser.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 §2.2, SEC-AU-14, §1.3. If a PUB operation rejects the cp-ssr scope (e.g. search.run for directory pages), SSR falls back to an anonymous token held by the server (DI-16).

amendments.change: Correction: the cp-ssr scope question is DI-14 (the 'DI-16' in the reason above is a typo). Anonymous tokens are DPoP-bound by the BFF: each pre-session holds its own ES256 key pair (server-side, in the session record) and every anonymous grant for that pre-session carries a DPoP proof made with it, so the backend's anonymous key (HMAC of cnf.jkt) stays the same across the 15-minute renewals. Without a proof the auth server gives every anonymous token a new random subject, so a guest's search sessions (search.page / search.refine), match sessions and rate-limit attribution would be lost at each renewal (DI-17). In lite mode the API does not check the binding; in strict mode the BFF adds a DPoP proof (htu = API URL, ath) to every API call made with a bound token. The token client takes a pluggable client-authentication strategy (none in lite; private_key_jwt over mTLS for cp-web-consumer and cp-ssr in strict mode, backend NI-01) and a PoW hook for the ATT anonymous grant in strict mode (DI-22).
amendments.reason: DI-17, DI-22, BA-26; verified in backend modules/identity/application/auth-ops.ts (#anonymous: subject uuidv7 unless DPoP) and libs/auth/authenticator.ts (anonKey from cnf.jkt ?? sub).

amendments.change: As built: SessionTokens (user refresh single-flight per session; anonymous grant per pre-session with one ES256 key in the session record) and SsrTokens (cp-ssr cached until 30 s before expiry; anonymous fallback with a process-wide key). The SSR fallback trigger is a 401 that persists after one fresh cp-ssr token. CarPal-Client always names the token's client (cp-ssr for cp-ssr tokens). Strict seams: ClientAuthentication (none | privateKeyJwt), DPoP proofs on API calls for bound tokens (htu = CARPAL_API_AUDIENCE + path), DPoP-Nonce retry at /oauth/token, PoW hook (CARPAL_STRICT_AUTH=1 = up front).

global_decisions.decision: BFF session store behind a port: lite = in-memory Map with TTL (single process, dev); full = Redis adapter (written, not verified, like the backend's full mode). Session cookie __Host-cp_sid (Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/), 256-bit random id, holds nothing but the id. CSRF: synchronizer token bound to the session, sent as X-CSRF-Token by the typed client on every non-GET call, plus Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin and Origin == app origin checks (SEC-WEB-3). The forwarder only allows the consumer audience from the generated registry (USR/PUB operations on the api host; no {org}, {adm} or fleet-manager paths) (SEC-WEB-5), strips cookies and browser-only headers, and passes CarPal-Retry-After-Ms / CarPal-Poll-After-Ms / retry_after_ms through unchanged (SEC-RL-5).
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 SEC-WEB-1..5, SEC-RL-5. The browser on http://localhost accepts Secure cookies (localhost is a secure context).

amendments.change: Allowlist rule made precise: the forwarder admits a route when it is on the api host and either (a) it has no {org_id} path parameter and one of its principal alternatives contains USR, PUB or LNK (160 operations), or (b) it is a /v1/orgs/{org_id}/fleet/… route whose principal alternatives contain DRV (18 operations: vehicles.list/get/mileage_add/mileage_list/status_history, issues.create/list/get/update, reminders.list, service_records.list/get, appointments.list/get/history/notes_list/check_in/delay) — fleet drivers use the consumer PWA (P12) and the backend checks the assignment per request (SEC-AZ-7, backend GD-20/GD-38). Auth-host operations are never forwarded by /api/v1 (they go through the /id proxy of GD-05). Media operations on single paths (USR | ORG(ANY)) fall under (a).
amendments.reason: BA-22; without (b) the P12 driver views could not reach their routes.

amendments.change: As built: 161 consumer routes + 18 DRV fleet routes are admitted (the '160 operations' of the alignment counted operations; one operation has two qualifying routes). Paths must be canonical (no dot segments, empty segments, encoded slashes/backslashes or non-ASCII); HEAD/OPTIONS are 405. Safe requests with Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site or same-site are refused too. The session record holds user tokens, the anonymous token, the DPoP key, pending logins (≤ 5, 30 min), intents (≤ 5, 30 min, ≤ 8 KiB) and a profile (display name from me.get); it is created lazily by /bff/csrf, /bff/login and the first /api/v1 call — /bff/session and SSR never create one. Updates are serialized per session id inside the process. The Redis adapter uses a built-in RESP2 client (no dependency), unverified.

global_decisions.decision: Data access: server components call the backend through a server-side typed client (same generated operation map) for public reads; client components use TanStack Query over the browser-side typed client that calls the BFF (/api/v1/...). The typed client adds Idempotency-Key (UUIDv7, kept across automatic retries) for IDEM operations and If-Match from the last ETag for ETAG operations, maps problem+json to typed errors (code catalog from the registry), and implements SEC-RL-4 once: honour retry/poll delays + 0-20 % jitter; otherwise exponential backoff with full jitter (base 500 ms, cap 30 s, 5 attempts) for safe methods and IDEM requests only; pause an operation after 3 consecutive 503s.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 §2.7 and §2.8 are client obligations 'enforced by contract tests'; centralizing them avoids every screen re-implementing them.

amendments.change: (1) ApiProblem carries the optional Problem members of Docs/40 §4.2: errors (FieldError list), requirements, consent_type, entitlement_key, safety (SafetyBlock & do_not_drive), fallback_path, vin_transfer_available (BA-03). (2) ETags are read from the ETag response header, never derived from a body version (questions carry no version in the body, backend DI-47); onboarding.update sends If-Match "v1" when no ETag is known for the flow (backend DI-14). (3) Automatic retries only when the server delay is ≤ 30 s; longer delays (e.g. the 3600 s of the appointment request caps, backend DI-55) are surfaced to the screen as a typed RateLimited error with the time, never slept on. (4) 400 CURSOR_MISMATCH on a page request means the cursor is no longer valid for this caller (e.g. a guest whose pre-session expired): the client re-runs the first page instead of showing an error. (5) A 412 VERSION_MISMATCH on a user edit becomes 'This changed elsewhere — reload' without losing input; reactions bump the version of posts and answers (backend S6), so the client refreshes the cached ETag after a reaction.

As built in src/lib/api/: createApiClient({ transport }) with api() (data) and call() (data + status, etag, pollAfterMs, replayed, requestId); browser transport to /api (api host) and /id (auth host); route choice by org_id; ApiProblem with every Problem member plus stepUp from WWW-Authenticate; automatic retries on 429/502/503/504 and network errors only (not 500, never AI_UNAVAILABLE); PAUSED after 3 consecutive 503s; CarPal-Poll-After-Ms pacing per operation+path; PoW on ATTESTATION_REQUIRED for the ATT operations; CURSOR_MISMATCH restart in useApiInfiniteQuery.

global_decisions.decision: i18n: i18next + react-i18next. Dictionaries live in shared/i18n/locales/{en,fa}.json (nested keys, namespaced per area) and are bundled into the PWA as the fallback; at runtime the PWA may fetch a newer version from config.client i18n.base_url/version and cache it. `pnpm i18n:check` fails if any en key is missing in fa (Docs/02 §3.1). Locale is the first URL segment (/fa, /en; default from region config = fa); <html lang dir> are set on the server. Dates use Intl with calendar 'persian' for fa (Jalali) and gregorian for en; digits follow the UI language (Intl 'fa' → Persian digits); plates, phones, codes and URLs stay as typed and are isolated with <bdi>. No date library unless Intl falls short (record it if added).

global_decisions.decision: Graceful degradation is part of every screen: 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED (backend not there yet), 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE, flags off in config.client (map.enabled, qna.enabled, community.*, ai.*, featured.enabled), 404 (never 403, SEC-AZ-2) and 410 each map to a defined UI state from Docs/21/22 ('not available yet', AI-off fallback, no access, removed). A screen never crashes or loops on them.
global_decisions.reason: The backend is mid-build (backend_readiness); Docs/40 SEC-AI-6 requires search, profiles and appointments to keep working without AI.

amendments.change: Re-weighted: 501 now only comes from auth.social_start (post-MVP, never called) and stays a defensive state. The degradations that will really happen are: (a) AI 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE — staging/prod run CARPAL_MCP_MODE=unavailable until the real MCP gateway exists (backend GD-35, NI-09), so the AI-off path is the expected pilot state, not an edge case; dev defaults to the deterministic stub; E2E covers both by starting the backend with CARPAL_MCP_MODE=unavailable for the AI-off suite; the triage 503 body carries safety and fallback_path (BA-02); (b) flags off by default in the seeds: community.feed.enabled, community.comments.enabled and qna.enabled are false (Should-have), featured.enabled false, map.enabled and the ai.* flags true (DI-18); (c) moderation holds: community text and Path 1 reviews with links, emails or phone numbers are held for the moderation queue (backend GD-22) and public media stay private until moderated, so 'Being reviewed' and media placeholders are normal states.

global_decisions.decision: Page URLs follow Docs/22 §6 except that they never carry free search text, coordinates, emails, phones, VINs or link tokens in the path or query (TR-7 spirit). Search pages are /<locale>/search/<search_session_id> plus enumerated filter params; the query text lives in the search session. Link tokens arrive in the fragment (/l/<type>#<token>, SEC-LT-2) and are POSTed. Help Me uses /<locale>/help/<session_id>/<step>.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 TR-7 and SEC-LT-2 vs. Docs/22 '/fa/search?…' (DI-05).

global_decisions.decision: Security of pages: nonce-based CSP set in Next.js middleware (script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; img-src self + media host + tile host; connect-src self + tile host), Trusted Types required, COOP/CORP same-origin, Permissions-Policy (geolocation=(self), camera=(self), others off), Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, HSTS in prod. All API text renders as text: dangerouslySetInnerHTML is banned by lint (except the JSON-LD script, built with a serializer that escapes '<'). Private pages send Cache-Control: no-store and robots noindex.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 SEC-WEB-4, SEC-IN-5, Docs/22 §6 (private pages never indexed).

amendments.change: As built (src/server/security-headers.ts via src/proxy.ts): script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-…' (no 'unsafe-inline'); img/media/connect-src add the storage origin and the map style origin; worker-src 'self'; frame-src, object-src, base-uri, frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script' with policies nextjs and nextjs#bundler in production only (dev adds 'unsafe-eval' and ws:); upgrade-insecure-requests and HSTS only on https (HSTS in prod). Private pages = /<locale>/{home,garage,help,appointments,review,settings,notifications,saved,activity}…, /id/*, /l/* → Cache-Control private, no-store + X-Robots-Tag noindex, nofollow. BFF responses carry no-store, nosniff, CORP same-origin and a sandbox CSP.
amendments.reason: P2.T8; verified in a production build with Playwright.

global_decisions.decision: Tests: Vitest + Testing Library (jsdom) for units and components (*.test.ts[x] next to the code); BFF integration tests (*.int.test.ts) run the BFF handlers against the live backend in lite mode; Playwright E2E (tests/e2e/) runs the built PWA against `pnpm dev` in backend/, Chromium only for now, with @axe-core/playwright on every visited page. E2E users sign up through the real hosted sign-in; one-time codes and email links are read from backend/.data/outbox-*.jsonl by a test helper (dev only). Tests use fresh emails under @test.carpal.app and assert only on their own data.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/02 WP19 tests (Playwright, RTL, accessibility); mirrors backend GD-13 (shared DB, own rows).

global_decisions.decision: Analytics: a small client queue batches registered events (search, map, directions, funnel; Docs/52 §18 names only) and sends them to events.ingest with platform 'web_pwa' (≤ 50 per request, on an interval and on visibilitychange). No personal data in properties. Cookie consent (Docs/22 §2.5) gates non-essential events. While the backend answers 501 (until backend S8), the queue drops events silently.
global_decisions.reason: Docs/40 §22.2 events.ingest, MVP §16 metrics, Docs/22 cookie consent.

conventions.naming: Screens are named by their Docs/22 id in a comment at the top of the page file (e.g. // W-GAR-01 My Garage (mirrors C-GARAGE-01/02/06/08/09)). API calls are made by operation id: api('vehicles.list', { query }) — never by hand-written paths.
ui_rules: Logical properties only (start/end, ms-/me-/ps-/pe-/start-/end-); lint forbids left/right utilities and properties.
User text: dir='auto' + unicode-bidi: plaintext; names, plates, numbers inside sentences in <bdi>.
Touch targets ≥ 48 px (tap-min); body 17 px; nothing under 13 px or weight 400.
Every icon-only button has an accessible label in the UI language; keyboard: '/' focuses search, Esc closes modals, visible focus ring (ring-focus).
Same trust language as mobile: badges, Verified visit / Approved by the business and CarPal labels, match reasons, AI suggestion labels (Docs/21 §2.3).
No Featured blocks rendered while featured.enabled is off; never on the map.
Copy: take EN/FA strings from mobile/preview/js/screens-*.js where a screen mirrors a mobile one; put them in shared/i18n under the area's namespace.
definition_of_done_per_screen: Route, layout per breakpoint (<768, 768-1199, ≥1200) and the elements of its Docs/22 entry (plus the Docs/21 element list for mirrored tools).
Every state listed in Docs/22/21 for the screen (loading skeleton, empty, error with Retry, 404/410, no access, 501/AI-off per GD-13).
EN and FA with correct direction; Daylight, Sunlight and Night themes.
Data only through the typed client; IDEM/ETAG handled by the client; gated actions go through the auth-intent modal (GD-06).
SEO for public pages (title, description, canonical, hreflang, JSON-LD, preview image, index/noindex per Docs/22 §6); no-store and noindex for private pages.
Tests: component tests for the view model/states; at least one Playwright path through the screen in EN or FA with an axe check (the key-flow E2E suites come in P13).

doc_issues.resolution: Checked: search.result_event takes 'viewed'|'selected' only, and the backend analytics registry (CLIENT_EVENTS) has no contact event. Ask the backend owner to register profile.contact_revealed {target_type, entry_point} (GD-17 amendment).

doc_issues.issue: Docs/22 W-NOTIF-01 offers consumer web push ('Get updates even when this tab is closed'); Docs/52 PushDeviceToken says web tokens serve provider and vendor portals and 'the consumer app does not receive business notifications'.

doc_issues.resolution: Checked: PushTokenRegister.platform includes 'web' for USR, and the backend dispatcher (modules/notification/application/dispatcher.ts) sends personal notifications to all of the user's tokens including web ones. Consumer web push is built in P12. Side effect recorded as DI-16.

doc_issues.action: The budget applies to the design-system component layer (ds/ + its CSS). Page budgets: LCP ≤ 2.5 s on a mid-range phone on 4G for public pages (Docs/22 principle 5), measured in P13.

doc_issues.action: Route /<locale>/parts/<vendor-slug>/<item_id>-<item-slug>; a wrong slug 301s to the canonical one. Same pattern as posts and questions.

doc_issues.issue: cp-ssr tokens carry scope public.read only; directory pages (W-PUB-04) and SSR question lists call search.run / questions.search (RL(search)), and the anonymous scope is 'public.read search'.
doc_issues.action: P5/P6 test whether the backend accepts cp-ssr for these; if not, SSR uses a server-held anonymous token (GD-07).
doc_issues.resolution: P2 checked live: the backend enforces no token scopes per operation, so cp-ssr may call search.run (and questions.search). ssrApi still falls back to a server-held anonymous token on 401. Rate-limit side effect recorded as DI-26.

doc_issues.issue: Region config map URLs (shared/region-config/ir-pilot.json) are placeholders; no tile build exists.
doc_issues.action: GD-12 fallback style; OQ-02.

doc_issues.issue: The backend dispatcher sends business notifications (organization context) to the user's web push tokens only, and a consumer PWA token and a portal token are both platform 'web' (backend GD-24). A user who is also a business member would get business pushes through the consumer PWA.
doc_issues.action: P12: the PWA service worker opens notifications with organization_context_id in the portal (URL from config) instead of a PWA route, and the in-app list filters them out (notifications.list without organization_id lists personal ones). Ask the backend owner to tell consumer and portal web tokens apart (e.g. a 'web_portal' platform or the CarPal-Client of the registering call).

doc_issues.issue: The anonymous grant gives cp-web-consumer a token with a random subject unless the request carries a DPoP proof; the backend derives the anonymous key from cnf.jkt ?? sub, so every 15-minute renewal would make a guest a new anonymous principal: earlier search sessions answer 404/400 CURSOR_MISMATCH, Discover/feed pages restart and rate limits are no longer per device. Docs/40 SEC-AU-14 says only that consumer web visitors get the token 'through the BFF session'.
doc_issues.action: GD-07 amendment: one ES256 DPoP key per BFF pre-session, used for every anonymous grant of that pre-session (and for API proofs in strict mode). Search pages also re-run the stored search request when a session is no longer readable (GD-09 amendment 4).
doc_issues.note: P2: built and verified against the live backend (bff.int.test.ts: a guest search session is still refinable after an anonymous renewal).

doc_issues.issue: community.feed.enabled, community.comments.enabled and qna.enabled are seeded off (Docs/43 seeds, Should-have), and the only way to change a flag is admin.flag_update on the admin plane (staff aal3 with a device-bound passkey, ETAG). P8 development and its E2E need them on, and the PWA must not write SQL.
doc_issues.action: P8.T0: add a small dev-only backend CLI (e.g. `pnpm dev:flags set <key> on|off`, refused unless CARPAL_ENV=dev) with a test, recorded in both plans (OQ-09 allows minimal backend changes). Until then the PWA shows the flag-off states (GD-13).

doc_issues.issue: Docs/22 W-SRCH-01 has mode tabs Showcases and Q&A, but search.run's showcases/qna modes rank providers (backend DI-48) and there is no showcase search operation.
doc_issues.action: P6: the Q&A tab calls questions.search (only when qna.enabled); the Showcases tab is hidden until a showcase search exists; listed in the P6 report.

doc_issues.issue: Organization slugs can change (≤ 2 per 30 days) and published organizations get a generated default slug ('<latin-name>-<12 hex>' or 'org-<12 hex>' for non-Latin names, backend S9b), but there is no slug history or redirect operation (backend DI-30): old /shop/<slug> links answer 404.

doc_issues.issue: P10.T5 planned the /l/ci check-in page 'for signed-in requester', but appointments.check_in_link is PUB LNK(ci): it works with the anonymous token too (backend S7: 'check-in by link needs an anonymous token like the other PUB link operations').
doc_issues.action: P10.T5 corrected (stage amendment): the page works for guests and signed-in users; LINK_EXPIRED 410 and INVALID_TRANSITION(outside_window) 409 states.

doc_issues.issue: Docs/40 types redirect_uri as Url, which is 'https:// only'; the backend rejects http://localhost redirect URIs (422 VALIDATION_FAILED /query/redirect_uri pattern). The plan's dev topology (GD-05) assumed http://localhost:3000.
doc_issues.action: GD-05 P2 amendment: register https://localhost:3000/bff/oauth/callback. P4 serves the PWA over https in development for the browser sign-in (OQ-10). P2 int tests drive the BFF directly with the https origin.

doc_issues.issue: auth.token and the /v1/auth/* sign-in operations are RL(auth.signin): 30 per 15 min per IP prefix (plus public.read 600/min per IP). The backend takes the client IP from the socket only, so behind the BFF every refresh, anonymous grant, code exchange and hosted-UI call of every user counts against the BFF host's one IP. In production this caps the whole site at about 30 sign-in-related calls per 15 minutes.
doc_issues.action: Tell the backend owner (noted in backend/dev_plan.json handoff_notes): the BFF needs a trusted forwarded client IP (e.g. a signed header accepted only from the BFF/mTLS) or confidential-client token requests exempt from the IP window. Until then the BFF keeps token calls to the minimum (lazy anonymous grants, single-flight refresh, no proactive refresh) and dev/test runs use CARPAL_RATE_LIMIT_SCALE=100.

doc_issues.issue: A cp-ssr token is an anonymous principal for the backend (acr anonymous, anonKey = HMAC(sub 'cp-ssr')), so all server rendering shares one public.read bucket (120/min, 3,000/day) and one search bucket (10/min anon). SEO pages (P5/P6) would hit that within minutes of real traffic.
doc_issues.action: Ask the backend owner for a cp-ssr bucket (or rate limiting cp-ssr per page host instead of per token). P5/P6 cache public reads on the server (short TTL) and measure the call count per page; record the result in their reports.

report.summary: P1 done. pwa/ is a hand-written Next.js 16 App Router package on the backend's local Node 24 (tools/use-local-node.{sh,ps1}, .node-version 24.21.0) with its own pnpm lockfile; shared/api-contracts (generated: operation map with routes, principals and parsed sec tags for all 406 operations / 458 routes, request/response types per operation, the 314 Docs/40 types plus the server-defined Json<…> shapes from openapi.yaml, enums, error codes, role groups), shared/i18n (EN/FA 'common' namespace, 19 keys) and shared/design-system/web (synced tokens, component CSS, fonts and licences) are linked packages or synced copies, each with a --check that fails on drift (verified by changing each source). The proxy redirects / and locale-less paths to the remembered, Accept-Language or region-default locale and stores ?theme= choices; the [locale] root layout sets <html lang dir data-theme>, links the design-system CSS from /ds and preloads only the current language's font. A placeholder home page (mirrors mobile S-AUTH-01: hero mark, word mark, promise, three trust points, language and theme links) and a localized 404 exist. Lint has two local rules (logical properties only; token-only values) plus a CSS checker, the dangerouslySetInnerHTML ban and the import boundaries; env is validated with zod at startup.

versions.prettier: 3.9.10 (backend style: single quotes, width 140, trailing commas, LF)
versions.yaml: 2.9.1 (reads openapi.yaml components in the contract generator)

deviations: Next.js 16 names middleware 'proxy' (src/proxy.ts) and runs it on the Node.js runtime; the plan's 'middleware' means this file (P2.T8 adds the security headers there).
tsconfig exactOptionalPropertyTypes is false: the plan said 'like backend', and backend/tsconfig.json has it false. allowJs is on so the tests can import the plain-JS tools.

Design-system files are served as static files from /ds (copied from shared/design-system/web into the gitignored public/ds by `sync-design-system.mjs --public`, run by `pnpm dev` and `pnpm build`) instead of being imported into the CSS bundle, so tokens.css stays byte-identical and the current language's font can be preloaded at a stable URL. P13 may add cache-busting for /ds.

Tailwind's default colour, spacing, radius, shadow, font, text, container and breakpoint scales are reset; utilities map only to tokens. Theme keys whose name equals a token name would be self-referencing, so radii, shadows and fonts use prefixed names (rounded-ds-md, shadow-ds-1, font-latin/font-persian); breakpoints are md 768 px and xl 1200 px (Docs/22).

Experimental Next.js flags: experimental.globalNotFound (the root layout is under the dynamic [locale] segment, so unmatched URLs get app/global-not-found.tsx with its own document) and experimental.turbopackAdditionalRoots (Turbopack root stays pwa/ and follows the pnpm links into ../shared; setting outputFileTracingRoot to the repository would have made the whole repo, including backend/.data, the Turbopack root).

notFound() thrown by a page renders, in Next.js 16.4.3, as an empty server shell (<html id="__next_error__">, status 404, localized title, noindex) and the [locale]/not-found.tsx body is drawn on the client; unmatched URLs are fully server-rendered by global-not-found.tsx. Checked against Next's app-render (Fizz cannot catch the not-found error inside the client boundary). See notes_for_next.
P1 already ported a partial Icon (car, wrench, check and the proposed shield, doc, globe) to src/components/ds/icon.tsx for the placeholder; P3.T1 completes it.

Theme choice without JavaScript: the proxy stores ?theme=light|sun|dark in the cp_theme cookie and redirects; the layout reads the cookie. P3.T3 adds prefers-contrast/prefers-color-scheme and the settings switch.
The minimal server translator getTranslator() (typed dotted keys over shared/i18n) stands in for i18next until P3.T2; keys stay.
The contract package covers all 406 operations (it is shared with the portals later); the consumer allowlist is derived from it in P2 (GD-08 amendment).
`next dev` writes pwa/AGENTS.md (pointer to the bundled Next.js docs); kept, since later stages benefit from it.

notes_for_next: Every command from pwa/ after `source tools/use-local-node.sh`. `pnpm check` runs everything except build and e2e; `pnpm e2e` builds and runs Playwright on port 3100 (next start), reusing a running server outside CI.

Read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before using a Next.js API: request APIs (params, cookies, headers) are async only; the proxy is src/proxy.ts; `pnpm typecheck` runs `next typegen` first (LayoutProps/PageProps helpers exist but P1 types params by hand).

Locale: the proxy guarantees the first path segment is fa or en and passes it to components without params as the x-carpal-locale request header (src/server/request-locale.ts). Its matcher skips /api, /bff, /id, /l, /_next, /ds and files with an extension — P2 adds /api/v1 and /bff route handlers and P4 the /id routes outside it, each needing its own root layout (only [locale] has one).

The generator reads backend/libs/contract/generated and, for x-server-schema types only, shared/api-contracts/openapi.yaml (sub-schemas get names like InsightPayload_triage_summary).

report.summary: P2 done. The consumer BFF lives in pwa/src/server/bff/ over standard Request/Response with no Next.js imports (GD-03, BA-23) and is mounted by thin route adapters: /api/v1/[...path] (forwarder), /bff/[...path] (login, oauth/callback, logout, session, csrf, intents), /id/oauth|v1|.well-known/[...path] (auth-host proxy of GD-05). The browser holds only __Host-cp_sid (Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; 256-bit id). Sessions sit behind a store port (lite in-memory TTL store; Redis adapter over a built-in minimal RESP client, unverified) with 12 h idle / 7 d absolute lifetimes, per-session serialized read-modify-write, and id rotation at sign-in. /bff/login starts authorization code + PKCE S256 with state and nonce through the same-origin /id proxy (ui_locales from the return URL; step-up = acr_values + prompt=login); the callback checks state (single use), the RFC 9207 iss parameter, exchanges the code server-to-server, verifies the ID token (EdDSA, JWKS from the internal auth URL, iss, aud, exp, nonce, required acr for step-up), calls me.get for the display name and rotates the session; logout revokes the refresh token. Tokens: user tokens refreshed single-flight per session (invalid_grant ends the user part of the session → 401 SESSION_ENDED); guests get a lazily created pre-session with one ES256 DPoP key that binds every anonymous grant (DI-17, verified live: a guest's search session stays readable across renewals); cp-ssr client-credentials cached process-wide with a server-held anonymous fallback (DI-14). The forwarder admits exactly the GD-08 audience (161 consumer routes + 18 DRV fleet routes from the registry; canonical paths only), enforces SEC-WEB-3 CSRF (X-CSRF-Token + Sec-Fetch-Site + Origin) on state changes and refuses cross-site reads, strips browser and backend headers both ways, passes retry/poll/ETag/WWW-Authenticate headers unchanged, renews a token once on 401 and repeats the call, and caps bodies at 64 KiB. The browser typed client (src/lib/api/) calls by operation id, picks the route (me vs fleet by org_id), adds Idempotency-Key (UUIDv7, reused across automatic retries) and If-Match from an ETag cache ("v1" for a first onboarding save), maps problem+json to ApiProblem with all Problem members and the step-up challenge, implements SEC-RL-4 (server delay + 0-20 % jitter, else full-jitter backoff 500 ms/30 s/5 attempts, safe methods and IDEM only, waits > 30 s surfaced, pause after 3 consecutive 503s) and SEC-RL-3 poll pacing, and solves PoW when an ATT operation is refused (Web Worker). TanStack Query helpers (ApiProvider, useApiQuery, useApiMutation, useApiInfiniteQuery with the CURSOR_MISMATCH restart), useSession, loginUrl, saveIntent/consumeIntent and useLogout are in place; server components get ssrApi(locale). The proxy now sets the GD-15 page headers on every page incl. /id and /l: per-request nonce CSP with 'strict-dynamic', Trusted Types enforced in production (Next.js's own 'nextjs' and 'nextjs#bundler' policies only), frame-ancestors/object-src/base-uri 'none', COOP/CORP same-origin, Permissions-Policy (geolocation and camera self only), Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options, HSTS in prod; private pages get private, no-store and X-Robots-Tag noindex. All P2 acceptance criteria verified: no token reaches the browser (unit and live int tests inspect every response), a fresh test user signs up and in through /bff/login → /id/oauth/authorize → /id/v1/auth/* → callback, calls me.get, refreshes after expiry and logs out (refresh token revoked at the auth server), CSRF/foreign-Origin state changes get 403, out-of-audience paths 404 without reaching the backend, IDEM retries reuse the key and 429 delays are honoured.

deviations: Docs/40 Url is https-only, so the backend rejects redirect_uri=http://localhost:3000/bff/oauth/callback (422 pattern). The plan's GD-05 dev values were http; they are now https (GD-05 P2 amendment). Guest browsing and the forwarder work on http://localhost:3000, but finishing a browser sign-in needs the PWA served over https: logged as DI-24, decision for P4 in OQ-10. The P2 integration tests call the BFF handlers directly with origin https://localhost:3000, so they need no TLS.

The /id proxy rewrites redirects that point at the issuer (https://id.carpal.app/...) or at the internal auth URL to <origin>/id/...; with that, CARPAL_SIGNIN_URL is optional in dev (the default <issuer>/signin lands on /id/signin). It forwards only the __Host-cp_ia cookie and returns only __Host-cp_ia Set-Cookies; /oauth/token and /oauth/revoke are not exposed to the browser (404). It also enforces Origin + Sec-Fetch-Site on state changes (a partial stand-in for DI-09 until the auth host checks them).

The callback reports failures to the page as ?signin=<outcome> on the return URL (expired | state | issuer | cancelled | failed | step_up); P4 renders the messages. No code, token or error description ever goes into the URL.

Pending intents (GD-06) are an API, not part of the login request: POST /bff/intents {type, target?, return_to, draft?} (≤ 8 KiB, ≤ 5 per session, 30 min), listed in /bff/session.pending_intents, consumed once with POST /bff/intents/<id>/consume. They are carried into the rotated session at sign-in.

The BFF passes STEP_UP_REQUIRED through unchanged (SEC-WEB-1: no added fields) together with the WWW-Authenticate challenge; the browser client parses acr_values/max_age from that header into ApiProblem.stepUp. BFF-generated problems use the contract shape with BFF codes CSRF_FAILED (403, with reason), SESSION_ENDED (401), BAD_GATEWAY (502/503) and INTERNAL (500).

Retries (GD-09): automatic retry statuses are 429, 502, 503, 504 and network errors; 500 is not retried, and 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE is never retried (it is a state, GD-13). A paused operation fails fast with code PAUSED and retryAfterMs. CURSOR_MISMATCH restarts are done by useApiInfiniteQuery (reset to the first page), not by every api() call.

CSP: Trusted Types are enforced only in production builds; next dev (React refresh, error overlay) assigns script URLs and HTML without a policy, so dev gets 'unsafe-eval', ws: and no Trusted Types. style-src has no 'unsafe-inline': server-rendered style="…" attributes would be blocked (P3 note). Verified in the built app: every Next.js script carries the nonce, hydration works, no CSP or Trusted Types violation in Chromium.

The proxy matcher now runs on /id/* and /l/* pages (security headers and noindex only, no locale routing) and still skips /api, /bff, /id/oauth, /id/v1, /id/.well-known, /_next, /ds and files; src/proxy.ts imports serverEnv (server-only) without problems in Next.js 16.4.3.

New env vars: CARPAL_API_AUDIENCE (DPoP htu of API calls, default https://api.carpal.app) and CARPAL_STRICT_AUTH (0|1; 1 = PoW up front for the anonymous grant). The BFF reports itself as CarPal-Client cp-web-consumer/<package.json version> (web 1.0); SSR calls use cp-ssr/<version>, or cp-web-consumer when they fall back to the anonymous token (CarPal-Client must equal the token's client_id).

DI-14 checked live: the backend does not enforce token scopes per operation, so a cp-ssr token can call search.run (200). The SSR client still falls back to the anonymous token on a 401 (after one fresh cp-ssr token). New concern DI-26: all cp-ssr calls share one anonymous rate-limit key.

P1 test tools/contract/generate.test.ts got a 30 s timeout: regenerating all 406 operations exceeded the 5 s default once while 21 test workers and the backend shared the machine (no drift; contract:check was green).
backend/: comment-only lines in backend/.env.example (the PWA dev env, P2.T3) and a handoff note in backend/dev_plan.json; no backend code changed.
notes_for_next: P3: wrap the app in <ApiProvider> (src/lib/api/query.tsx) in the [locale] layout or the app shell; P2 did not touch the layouts. Client code imports '@/lib/api' (core), '@/lib/api/query' (hooks) and '@/lib/api/session' (useSession, loginUrl, saveIntent, consumeIntent, useLogout). Server components use ssrApi(locale).api(opId, …) from '@/server/ssr/api'.

SameSite=Strict means the first navigation from another site (a search engine, an email link) arrives WITHOUT the session cookie, so server rendering sees a guest even for a signed-in user. The (app) layout must not redirect to sign-in on the server just because the cookie is missing: render the shell and let the client confirm with /bff/session (same-origin fetches do carry the cookie), or do a same-origin reload. Decide this in P3/P4 and record it.

P4 needs HTTPS for a real browser sign-in (DI-24, OQ-10): backend redirect URIs must be https. Options: `next dev --experimental-https` (mkcert installs a local CA — ask the user first) or a local TLS proxy; then set CARPAL_PWA_ORIGIN=https://localhost:3000, CARPAL_SIGNIN_URL=https://localhost:3000/id/signin and the redirect URI of README. Playwright then needs ignoreHTTPSErrors or the CA.

P4 hosted UI: call auth-host operations through the same client (api('auth.signin_password', …) goes to /id/v1/auth/signin with the interaction cookie); ATT operations solve PoW automatically when refused. Completion = navigate to the same /id/oauth/authorize URL the browser came from (keep it from the first request; the callback is /bff/oauth/callback). Show ?signin=<outcome> messages on the return page.

Step-up: catch ApiProblem.stepUp (401 STEP_UP_REQUIRED) → save the action with saveIntent() → location = loginUrl({ stepUp: problem.stepUp.acrValues }) → on return consumeIntent() and replay. SESSION_ENDED (401) means the BFF dropped the user: refresh the session view (ApiProvider does it) and show the signed-out state.

CSP: nonces need dynamic rendering (the [locale] layout reads cookies, so every page is dynamic today); a statically rendered page would ship scripts without the nonce and break. Any library that sets script URLs or HTML (MapLibre workers in P6, a service worker in P12) must get its Trusted Types policy name added to TRUSTED_TYPES_POLICIES in src/server/security-headers.ts and, for blob workers, worker-src blob: — test in a production build (dev does not enforce Trusted Types). No style attributes in server-rendered markup unless style-src-attr is added deliberately.

Map tiles and media: the CSP img-src/media-src/connect-src take CARPAL_STORAGE_URL and the origin of CARPAL_PWA_MAP_STYLE_URL; a tile host from config.client (GD-12) must be added there too when P6 uses it.

Rate limits (DI-25): every BFF token call and every hosted-UI /v1/auth/* call reaches the auth host from one IP, and auth.signin allows 30 per 15 min per IP prefix. Keep CARPAL_RATE_LIMIT_SCALE=100 for local test runs and expect 429s on a shared dev backend otherwise. The BFF passes the 429/503 delay to the browser (BAD_GATEWAY with retry_after_ms for token-endpoint backpressure).

test:int needs the backend: `pnpm dev` in backend/ with the env in pwa/README.md (https redirect URI, CARPAL_RATE_LIMIT_SCALE=100). It signs fresh @test.carpal.app users up and reads backend/.data/outbox-mail.jsonl for the verification link. The e2e test that forwards to the backend skips itself when the backend is down.

Redis store (OQ-06): refresh single-flight is per process. With several PWA instances behind the Redis store, two instances can refresh the same session at once and the second use trips refresh-reuse detection (family revoked → user signed out). Before multi-instance production, add a distributed lock (SET NX PX) around refresh or pin sessions to an instance.
Analytics (GD-17) and the PoW worker: src/lib/api/pow.worker.ts is loaded with new Worker(new URL(…)); if a Trusted Types or CSP refusal blocks it the solver falls back to the main thread in slices.
